overview.h1: HTS Chapter 75: Nickel and Articles Thereof — 2026 Tariff Rates

seo.title: HTS Chapter 75 Nickel Tariffs: HS Codes, Import Duties & 2026 Section 301 Rates | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Searchable U.S. duty table for all 29 HTS Chapter 75 nickel lines: unwrought nickel, scrap and powders are Free and exempt from the 2026 Section 301 tariffs; nickel alloy bar, wire, sheet and tube pay 2% to 3% plus 10% to 12.5%. No Section 232 duty; China 25% to 40.5%.

overview.intro:
Chapter 75 covers nickel from the smelter to the finished article: nickel mattes and oxide sinters (7501), **unwrought nickel** such as cathode and briquettes (7502), **scrap** (7503), **powders** (7504), and the wrought products made from pure nickel and nickel alloys: bars, rods and **wire** (7505), plates, **sheet**, strip and foil (7506), **tubes** and fittings (7507) and other articles (7508). Base rates are low: Free for the raw forms, 2% to 3% for the rest.

**No Section 232 duty reaches nickel.** The processed critical minerals investigation ended in January 2026 with negotiations, not tariffs (Proclamation 11001), and the steel, aluminum and copper programs list no Chapter 75 line. What decides the cost today is the **2026 Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** (from July 24, 2026): +10% or +12.5% for most suppliers, or a 10% or 12.5% floor for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan. Unwrought nickel, mattes, scrap, powders and other articles (7508.90.50) are on its exemption list (note 52(b)), so they stay Free; bars, wire, sheet, tube and fittings pay it. USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt. China pays **25%** under Section 301 on every line; Russian nickel pays column 2 or 35% rates and, if produced on or after April 13, 2024, **cannot be imported** at all under a Treasury (OFAC) determination.

No antidumping or countervailing duty order covers Chapter 75 goods.

productGroups.label: Nickel mattes & oxide sinters
productGroups.blurb: Nickel mattes and nickel oxide sinters and other intermediate products of nickel smelting: 2 lines, Free. Mattes (7501.10) are on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list; oxide sinters (7501.20) are not, so they pay 10% to 12.5% from the 60 Section 301 economies.

productGroups.label: Unwrought nickel (cathode, briquettes, alloys)
productGroups.blurb: Unwrought nickel, not alloyed (cathode, briquettes, rounds, pellets) and unwrought nickel alloys: 2 lines, Free. On the 2026 Section 301 and Brazil exemption lists, so only China (25%) and Russia (35%) pay a duty.

productGroups.label: Nickel waste & scrap
productGroups.blurb: Nickel and nickel-alloy waste and scrap, including superalloy turnings and solids: 1 line, Free. On the 2026 Section 301 exemption list; only China (25%) and Russia (column 2) pay extra.

productGroups.label: Nickel powders & flakes
productGroups.blurb: Nickel powders and flakes, used in batteries, powder metallurgy, catalysts and thermal spray: 2 lines, Free. On the 2026 Section 301 exemption list; China pays 25%, Russia 35%.

productGroups.label: Nickel bars, rods, profiles & wire
productGroups.blurb: Bars, rods, profiles and wire of pure nickel and nickel alloys (nickel-chromium, nickel-copper and other high-performance alloys), cold-formed or not: 10 lines at 2.5% to 3%, Free under most FTAs and USMCA. The 2026 Section 301 duty applies.

productGroups.label: Nickel plates, sheets, strip & foil
productGroups.blurb: Plates, sheets, strip and foil of pure nickel and nickel alloys, including foil not over 0.15 mm thick: 6 lines at 2.5% or 3%. The 2026 Section 301 duty applies; Russian nickel-alloy sheet (7506.20.30) pays 35% in lieu of column 2.

productGroups.label: Nickel tubes, pipes & fittings
productGroups.blurb: Tubes and pipes of pure nickel and nickel alloys, and tube or pipe fittings (couplings, elbows, sleeves): 3 lines at 2% or 3%. The 2026 Section 301 duty applies.

productGroups.label: Other articles of nickel
productGroups.blurb: Cloth, grill and netting of nickel wire, stranded wire, and other articles of nickel such as anodes for plating, electroforms and fasteners: 3 lines at 3%. 7508.90.50 (other articles) is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list.

workedExamples.title: $1,000,000 of nickel cathode from Canada or Norway
workedExamples.body: Unwrought, unalloyed nickel is **Free**, and 7502.10 is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list (note 52(b), heading 9903.05.86), so the 10% (Canada) or 12.5% (Norway) duty does not apply. No Section 232 duty reaches nickel. The duty is **$0**, with or without a USMCA claim.

workedExamples.title: Nickel alloy bar from Germany
workedExamples.body: Cold-formed nickel-alloy bar is 3%. For goods of the EU the 2026 Section 301 rate (9903.05.39) is a **10% floor**: it replaces the base rate when the base rate is lower. The total is **10%**: $10,000 on $100,000.

workedExamples.title: The same bar from the United Kingdom
workedExamples.body: 3% base **+ 10%** Section 301 (9903.05.81) = **13%**: $13,000 on $100,000. The UK rate is added to the base rate instead of replacing it.

workedExamples.title: Nickel alloy pipe from Mexico, with and without a USMCA claim
workedExamples.body: 2% base. With a valid USMCA claim the base rate is Free and the 10% Section 301 duty is lifted (note 52(h), heading 9903.05.94): **$0**. Without it: 2% **+ 10%** (9903.05.55) = **12%**.

workedExamples.title: Nickel scrap and nickel alloy sheet from China
workedExamples.body: Cold-formed nickel-alloy sheet: 3% base **+ 25%** Section 301 List 3 (9903.88.03) **+ 12.5%** 2026 Section 301 (9903.05.31) = **40.5%**. Nickel scrap (7503.00.00.00) is Free and exempt from the 12.5%, so it pays **25%**.

workedExamples.title: Unwrought nickel from Russia
workedExamples.body: Nickel of Russian origin produced on or after **April 13, 2024 may not be imported** (OFAC determination under Executive Order 14068). Nickel produced earlier pays **35%** in lieu of the 6.6¢/kg column 2 rate (9903.90.08, U.S. note 30(b), from April 1, 2023); 7502.10 is exempt from the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on Russia.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Subheading note 1 (definitions).** (a) *Nickel, not alloyed*: metal with at least 99% nickel plus cobalt by weight, provided cobalt does not exceed 1.5%, iron 0.5%, oxygen 0.4% and any other element 0.3%. (b) *Nickel alloys*: metallic substances in which nickel predominates by weight over each other element, provided cobalt exceeds 1.5%, or at least one other element exceeds its limit in the table, or the elements other than nickel plus cobalt total more than 1%.

**Subheading note 2.** Despite note 9(c) to Section XV, for subheading 7508.10 "wire" means products, coiled or not, of any cross-section, with no cross-sectional dimension over 6 mm.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 75 Tariff Updates: Nickel Tariffs 2025–2026

seo.title: Nickel Tariff Updates 2026: Section 301, Critical Minerals 232, Russia, China (HTS Ch. 75) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Every change to U.S. tariffs on nickel (HTS Chapter 75) since January 2025, with official sources: the end of the IEEPA tariffs and the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs and their nickel exemptions, the critical minerals Section 232 decision (no tariff), China Section 301 and Russian nickel.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule, the **2025 Basic Edition** (in force January 1, 2025) and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026), and lists every extra duty that reaches Chapter 75 today. Base rates did not change: all 29 lines carry the same general rate in both editions.

The extra duties changed several times. In 2025 nickel paid the IEEPA duties: the reciprocal tariff on wrought nickel (unwrought nickel, mattes, scrap and powders were on its Annex II exemption list) and the Canada, Mexico and China duties. The IEEPA tariffs **ended on February 24, 2026**; a 10% Section 122 surcharge replaced them until **July 23, 2026**, with the same nickel exemptions. Since **July 24, 2026** the **2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies** (10% or 12.5%) charge 22 of 29 lines, and Brazil pays a further 25%. The processed critical minerals **Section 232** investigation ended with negotiations and **no tariff** (Proclamation 11001, January 14, 2026). China's 2018 Section 301 duty (25%) continues.

Russian nickel is a special case: column 2 rates since April 2022, 35% in lieu of column 2 on unwrought nickel and powders since April 1, 2023, and an import ban on nickel produced on or after April 13, 2024. No antidumping or countervailing duty order covers Chapter 75 goods.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 75 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 actions on 60 economies and Brazil (notes 50, 52), China Section 301 (note 20), Russia's rates in lieu of column 2 (note 30), the scheduled Nicaragua Section 301 duty (note 29), and the ended IEEPA and Section 122 duties. No Section 232 note (16 and the others) lists a Chapter 75 line, and Canada's Section 338 lists (note 51) contain none. Treasury's import prohibition on Russian nickel is included because it decides whether Russian nickel can enter at all. A Federal Register search found no Commerce antidumping or countervailing duty order on Chapter 75 goods. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

stats.label: 2026 Section 301
stats.note: 22 lines; unwrought nickel, scrap and powders exempt

inEffect.country: 60 Section 301 economies (Canada, the UK, the EU, Norway, Japan, Mexico, Australia, South Africa, Taiwan, Korea, India and others)
inEffect.now: +10% or +12.5%; for the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan a 10% or 12.5% floor in place of the base rate
inEffect.exemption: Charges 22 of 29 lines: nickel bars, rods, wire, plates, sheet, strip, foil, tubes, fittings, cloth, stranded wire and oxide sinters (7501.20). Nickel mattes (7501.10), unwrought nickel (7502.10, 7502.20), scrap (7503), powders and flakes (7504) and other articles of nickel (7508.90.50) are on the note 52(b) exemption list (9903.05.86). USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico entered free of duty are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). No Chapter 75 line is on a note 52(j) country exception list, and no Section 232 action reaches nickel, so note 52(f) does not apply. Rates: Canada, Mexico, the UK and India +10%; Norway, Australia, South Africa, Brazil, China and Russia +12.5%; EU 10% and Taiwan 10%, Japan and Korea 12.5%, in place of the base rate when it is lower. Foreign-trade-zone admissions must take privileged foreign status.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Nickel alloy bar, wire, sheet or tube from the UK costs 12% to 13% instead of 2% to 3%; from the EU or Japan 10% or 12.5%. Nickel cathode, scrap and powder stay Free.

inEffect.now: +25% on all 29 lines, +12.5% more on the 22 non-exempt lines
inEffect.exemption: List 3 (note 20(f)) names every Chapter 75 subheading. No product exclusion is in force: the exclusions for nickel hydroxy carbonate (7501.20.0000) expired June 14, 2024. The 12.5% 2026 duty (9903.05.31) does not charge the six note 52(b) subheadings. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026; USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018 actions continue during the four-year review.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese nickel cathode, scrap and powder pay 25%; Chinese nickel alloy bar, wire, sheet and tube 39.5% to 40.5%.

inEffect.exemption: The Brazil exemption list (note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03) names the same six Chapter 75 subheadings as note 52(b): mattes, unwrought nickel, scrap, powders and 7508.90.50. They pay neither duty.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian unwrought nickel stays Free; Brazilian nickel alloy semis pay 39.5% to 40.5%.

inEffect.measure: Column 2 rates, 35% in lieu of column 2 on 5 lines, +12.5% Section 301; import ban on nickel produced since April 13, 2024
inEffect.before: Column 2 rates; 35% in lieu of column 2 on 5 lines
inEffect.now: 35% on unwrought nickel and powders; column 2 (25% to 45%) + 12.5% on semis; 47.5% on nickel-alloy sheet 7506.20.30
inEffect.exemption: Russia has paid column 2 rates since April 9, 2022. Note 30(b) puts 35% in lieu of column 2 on 7506.20.30 (from July 27, 2022, Proclamation 10420) and on 7502.10, 7502.20 and 7504 (from April 1, 2023, Proclamation 10523). The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.66) is added on the 22 non-exempt lines. Separately, OFAC determined on April 12, 2024 that the import prohibition of Executive Order 14068 applies to nickel of Russian Federation origin, except nickel produced before April 13, 2024 or licensed by OFAC (31 CFR part 587). No revocation has been published in the Federal Register.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Newly produced Russian nickel cannot be imported. Older stock pays 35% (unwrought, powders) or up to 57.5% (semis and articles).

changes.title: No Chapter 75 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 29 Chapter 75 lines carry the same general rate in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; none changed and none are new or renumbered.

changes.title: No antidumping or countervailing duty order on Chapter 75 goods
changes.detail: A Federal Register search of Commerce (ITA) notices finds no AD/CVD order on nickel or nickel-alloy products of Chapter 75. The only order with nickel in its name, on diffusion-annealed nickel-plated flat-rolled steel from Japan (preliminary review results published August 5, 2026), covers a steel product of Chapter 72, not nickel.

changes.title: China Section 301 duties continue during the review
changes.detail: USTR announced that the 2018–2019 Section 301 actions on China, including List 3 (25%) that covers all 29 Chapter 75 lines, continue while the statutory four-year review proceeds.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duties: no Chapter 75 line
changes.detail: Proclamations 11046–11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.12–9903.03.14) on Canadian products in the note 51(b) lists from August 22, 2026, with lists changed from September 15, 2026. No Chapter 75 line is on any list, so Canadian nickel, the largest source, is unaffected.

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies reach 22 nickel lines
changes.detail: The 10% or 12.5% duties on goods of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) took effect, with a 10% or 12.5% floor in place of the base rate for the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan. Nickel mattes, unwrought nickel, scrap, powders and 7508.90.50 are on the note 52(b) exemption list (9903.05.86); USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt. The other 22 lines (bars, rods, wire, sheet, strip, foil, tubes, fittings, cloth, stranded wire and oxide sinters) pay it.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Brazil
changes.detail: The 25% duty on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) took effect. The same six Chapter 75 subheadings as note 52(b) are on its exemption list (note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03); the other 22 lines pay it, plus the 12.5% 2026 duty from July 24.

changes.title: USTR asks for comments on a critical minerals agreement
changes.detail: Following Proclamation 11001, USTR requested public comments on the design of a plurilateral agreement on trade in critical minerals, including price floors and other measures. No tariff on nickel has resulted.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: A 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) applied until July 23, 2026. Nickel mattes, unwrought nickel, scrap, powders and 7508.90.50 were on its product exemption list (9903.03.03), and USMCA-qualifying goods of Canada and Mexico were exempt; the other 22 lines paid it.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 on processed critical minerals: negotiations, no tariff
changes.detail: Proclamation 11001 agreed with Commerce that imports of processed critical minerals and their derivative products, which it says include nickel used in battery storage, threaten national security, but directed Commerce and USTR to negotiate agreements (considering price floors) instead of imposing tariffs, with an update due within 180 days. No Section 232 duty applies to Chapter 75, and no later proclamation has been published as of October 13, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29), on all 29 Chapter 75 lines. The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: IEEPA duty on China cut to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14357 lowered the IEEPA duty on products of China from 20% to 10% from November 10, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods raised to 35%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14325 raised the IEEPA duty on Canadian goods not entered under USMCA from 25% to 35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 investigation of processed critical minerals opens
changes.detail: Executive Order 14272 directed Commerce to investigate imports of processed critical minerals and their derivative products; Commerce opened the investigation on April 22, 2025 and took comments until May 16, 2025. It ended with Proclamation 11001 (no tariff).

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff: unwrought nickel, scrap and powders exempt
changes.detail: Executive Order 14257 set the reciprocal tariffs from April 5, 2025, with an Annex II exemption list (9903.01.32) that, as printed in the current schedule, includes nickel mattes, unwrought nickel, scrap, powders and 7508.90.50. Nickel bars, wire, sheet, tube and the other wrought lines paid the reciprocal rate. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: IEEPA duty on China raised to 20%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14228 raised the IEEPA duty on products of China (9903.01.20) from 10% to 20%, on top of the Section 301 duties. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: IEEPA duties on Canada, Mexico and China
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada (9903.01.10) and Mexico (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025, with USMCA goods exempted from March 7, 2025; +10% on goods of China (9903.01.20) from February 4, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Import ban on Russian nickel
changes.detail: OFAC determined that the import prohibition of Executive Order 14068 applies to aluminum, copper and nickel of Russian Federation origin, including admission into a foreign-trade zone, except metal produced before April 13, 2024 or licensed by OFAC. It also barred U.S. persons from warranting Russian nickel on a metal exchange. Published in the Federal Register on June 6, 2024.

changes.title: Russian unwrought nickel and powders: 35% in lieu of column 2
changes.detail: Proclamation 10523 added unwrought nickel (7502.10, 7502.20) and nickel powders and flakes (7504) to U.S. note 30(b), so they pay 35% (9903.90.08) instead of the 6.6¢/kg column 2 rate.

changes.title: Russian nickel-alloy sheet: 35% in lieu of column 2
changes.detail: Proclamation 10420 created heading 9903.90.08 and U.S. note 30 and raised the rate on listed Russian products, including nickel-alloy plates, sheets and strip not cold-formed (7506.20.30), to 35% in lieu of column 2. Russia has paid column 2 rates since April 9, 2022 under the Suspending Normal Trade Relations with Russia and Belarus Act.

changes.title: China List 3 raised to 25%
changes.detail: The List 3 duty on Chinese nickel (every Chapter 75 line), 10% from September 24, 2018, rose to 25%.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 75 nickel were **$3.37B in 2025**, -6.9% from $3.62B in 2024 and down from the 2022 peak of $4.50B. **Unwrought nickel (7502) was $1.39B**, 41% of the total: Canada shipped $785M, Norway $233M, the United Kingdom $112M, South Africa $76M, Japan $54M and Finland $43M. Scrap was $350M (the UK $106M, Canada $67M, Mexico $40M) and powders $103M, mostly from Canada. These raw forms ($1.87B, 55%) are on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, except nickel oxide sinters (7501.20, $23M with mattes).

Wrought nickel and nickel alloys were $1.50B: other articles (7508) $532M, led by Mexico ($100M); bars, rods and wire (7505) $521M, led by France ($114M), Germany ($97M) and Australia ($70M); tubes and fittings (7507) $267M; and sheet, strip and foil (7506) $184M, led by Germany and Japan. These are the goods that pay the 2026 Section 301 duty, except USMCA goods and 7508.90.50.

No Chapter 75 imports from Russia were recorded in 2025; Russian nickel produced since April 13, 2024 may not be imported. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Nickel ores (Chapter 26), ferronickel (Chapter 72) and nickel chemicals (Chapter 28) are not included. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duties for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. For the raw forms the answer is simple: **unwrought nickel, mattes, scrap and powders are Free** from every listed country except China (25%) and Russia, because they are on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list.

For the wrought products (bars, rods, wire, plates, sheet, strip, foil, tubes and fittings) the 2026 Section 301 tariff decides the rate: **Free** for USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico, **10%** for the EU and Taiwan and **12.5%** for Japan and Korea (floors that replace the base rate), base rate **+10%** for the UK and India, and **+12.5%** for Norway, Australia and South Africa (whose base rate is Free under their FTA or AGOA). China and Brazil pay about 40%. No Section 232 duty and no antidumping or countervailing duty applies to Chapter 75.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 75: Nickel and Articles Thereof — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Nickel: Section 301 Exemptions, USMCA, Russian Nickel Ban & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 75) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 75 nickel line: the 2026 Section 301 exemption list for unwrought nickel, scrap and powders, USMCA certification, FTZ status, marking and the OFAC ban on Russian nickel, plus the legal ways to pay less: buying unwrought forms, USMCA and FTA claims, non-Chinese origin, correct alloy classification and drawback.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For nickel the classification and the origin decide almost everything. Six subheadings, **nickel mattes (7501.10), unwrought nickel (7502.10, 7502.20), scrap (7503), powders and flakes (7504) and other articles (7508.90.50)**, are on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list and Free, so they pay nothing except from China or Russia. The other 22 lines, the wrought nickel and nickel-alloy products, pay a 2% to 3% base rate and the 10% to 12.5% Section 301 duty of most suppliers. There is no Section 232 duty and no AD/CVD order on Chapter 75.

The legal ways to pay less: buy nickel in an exempt form and fabricate it in the United States, claim USMCA for Canadian and Mexican goods (it removes both the base rate and the Section 301 duty), claim an FTA or AGOA for the base rate, avoid Chinese origin, classify the alloy and form correctly, and claim drawback on exported goods. Russian nickel produced since April 13, 2024 cannot be imported. Each rule and lever links to its regulation or legal text.

levers.title: Import unwrought nickel, scrap or powder and fabricate in the United States
levers.saves: The 10% to 12.5% Section 301 duty and the 2% to 3% base rate: 7502, 7503 and 7504 are Free and on the note 52(b) exemption list
levers.appliesTo: Cathode, briquettes, unwrought alloys, scrap, powders and flakes (7502–7504), instead of bars, wire, sheet or tube (7505–7507)
levers.document: Mill or assay certificates and a product description showing the goods are unwrought, scrap or powder (19 CFR 141.86 invoice description).
levers.caveat: Only real changes in what you buy count: nickel rolled, drawn or extruded abroad is 7505–7507. Chinese goods still pay 25% (List 3) in any form.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(b)

levers.title: Claim USMCA for Canadian and Mexican nickel
levers.saves: The base rate (2% to 3%) and the 10% Section 301 duty: USMCA goods entered free of duty are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94)
levers.appliesTo: Originating nickel products of Canada and Mexico, mainly bars, wire, sheet, tube, fittings and other articles
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin (19 CFR 182.12), kept on file and presented when CBP asks.
levers.caveat: The good must meet the USMCA rule of origin for its heading; non-originating Canadian or Mexican semis pay 12% to 13%.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(g)–(h)

levers.title: Claim an FTA or AGOA rate for the base duty
levers.saves: The 2% to 3% base rate on semis
levers.appliesTo: Originating goods of Australia (AU), Korea (KR), Chile, Colombia, Peru, Israel, Singapore and other FTA partners, and AGOA countries such as South Africa (D)
levers.document: The agreement's certification or proof of origin, kept on file and presented when CBP asks.
levers.caveat: An FTA or AGOA claim does not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(a)): Australian or South African nickel-alloy bar still pays 12.5%. GSP has lapsed.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Avoid Chinese and Russian origin
levers.saves: 25% of value on every line, plus 12.5% on semis: Chinese nickel pays 25% to 40.5% against Free to 15.5% from other countries
levers.appliesTo: All 29 lines, for goods of China; Russian nickel produced since April 13, 2024 cannot be imported
levers.document: Mill certificates and production records showing where the nickel was smelted, refined and worked. Origin follows the last substantial transformation; ask CBP for a binding ruling if processing happens in more than one country.
levers.caveat: Simple processing in a third country does not change origin. OFAC's prohibition covers Russian-origin nickel wherever it is shipped from.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 20

levers.title: Classify the alloy and the form correctly
levers.saves: The Section 301 duty when a product is truly unwrought, scrap or powder, and the right base rate for bars, wire, sheet and tube
levers.appliesTo: All lines; most often nickel alloy vs other base-metal alloys, unwrought vs wrought, and 7508.90.50 (exempt) vs 7508.10 and 7508.90.10
levers.document: A chemical analysis against subheading note 1 (nickel must predominate by weight) and Section XV note 5, a description of form and processing, and if unsure a CBP binding ruling.
levers.caveat: Classification follows the product, not the duty: an alloy in which iron predominates (stainless or alloy steel) is Chapter 72 or 73, and nickel oxides and sulfate are Chapter 28.

levers.title: Claim drawback on exported goods
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the base rate and Section 301 duties paid on goods that are exported or used in exported products
levers.document: A drawback claim to CBP with import and export records (19 CFR part 191).
levers.caveat: Antidumping and countervailing duties are never refundable (19 CFR 191.3(b)(3)); none apply to Chapter 75 today.

keyTakeaways: Unwrought nickel, mattes, scrap, powders and other articles (7508.90.50) are Free and on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list: they pay no duty except from China (25%) and Russia.

Wrought nickel and nickel alloys (bars, wire, sheet, strip, foil, tubes, fittings) pay 2% to 3% plus the 2026 Section 301 duty of most suppliers: 10% (EU floor), 12.5% (Japan, Korea), 12% to 13% (UK), Free with USMCA, about 40% from China and Brazil.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on nickel?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on nickel
faqs.answer: Unwrought nickel (cathode, briquettes), nickel mattes, scrap and powders are Free and on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, so they pay no duty from almost every country; China pays 25% and Russian nickel is restricted. Wrought nickel and nickel alloys (bars, rods, wire, plates, sheet, strip, foil, tubes and fittings) pay a 2% to 3% base rate plus the 2026 Section 301 duty of most suppliers: 10% to 15.5% in total, or Free with a USMCA claim. There is no Section 232 duty on nickel.

faqs.question: Is nickel subject to a Section 232 or critical minerals tariff?
faqs.answer: No. Commerce investigated processed critical minerals under Section 232 from April 2025, and Proclamation 11001 (January 14, 2026) found a threat to national security but chose negotiations with trading partners, considering price floors, instead of tariffs. No Section 232 note in the tariff schedule lists a Chapter 75 line, and the steel, aluminum and copper duties do not cover nickel. No later proclamation had been published as of October 13, 2026.

faqs.question: Which nickel products are exempt from the 2026 tariffs?
faqs.answer: Six subheadings are on the exemption list of the 2026 Section 301 tariffs (note 52(b), 9903.05.86) and of the Brazil tariff: nickel mattes (7501.10), unwrought nickel not alloyed and alloyed (7502.10, 7502.20), nickel waste and scrap (7503.00), powders and flakes (7504.00) and other articles of nickel (7508.90.50). The same six were exempt from the 2025 reciprocal tariff and the 2026 Section 122 surcharge. They are not exempt from China's 25% Section 301 duty.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for nickel?
faqs.answer: Unwrought nickel is heading 7502: 7502.10.00.00 for nickel not alloyed (cathode, briquettes, pellets, at least 99% nickel plus cobalt) and 7502.20.00.00 for nickel alloys. Mattes and oxide sinters are 7501, scrap 7503, powders 7504. Nickel ores are 2604.00.00, nickel oxides 2825.40, nickel sulfate 2833.24 and ferronickel 7202.60, outside Chapter 75.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for nickel alloy bar, wire, plate and tube?
faqs.answer: Nickel-alloy bars and rods are 7505.12 (3% or 2.5%), wire 7505.22 (3% or 2.6%), plates, sheet, strip and foil 7506.20 (2.5% or 3%), tubes and pipes 7507.12 (2%) and fittings 7507.20 (3%). Pure nickel uses 7505.11, 7505.21, 7506.10 and 7507.11. An alloy is a nickel alloy only if nickel predominates by weight (subheading note 1).

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on Inconel and other nickel alloys?
faqs.answer: Nickel-chromium superalloys in which nickel predominates are Chapter 75 nickel alloys: bar 7505.12, wire 7505.22, sheet 7506.20, tube 7507.12. They pay a 2% to 3% base rate plus the 2026 Section 301 duty: 10% from the EU, 12.5% from Japan, 12% to 13% from the UK, Free with USMCA, about 40% from China. Their scrap (7503) and unwrought ingots (7502.20) are Free.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for nickel powder?
faqs.answer: Nickel powders and flakes are 7504.00.00 (statistical suffix .10 powders, .50 flakes), Free and on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list. Chinese powder pays 25%; Russian powder 35% in lieu of column 2.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for nickel scrap, and is there a tariff?
searchedAs: nickel waste and scrap hs code
faqs.answer: Nickel and nickel-alloy waste and scrap is 7503.00.00.00. It is Free and on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, so it pays no duty except from China (25%) and Russia (6.6¢/kg column 2).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for nickel matte?
faqs.answer: Nickel mattes are 7501.10.00.00 and nickel oxide sinters and other intermediate products of nickel metallurgy 7501.20.00.00; both are Free. Mattes are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty; oxide sinters are not. Chemical nickel oxides and hydroxides are 2825.40.00.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on nickel from Canada?
searchedAs: how much nickel does the us import from canada
faqs.answer: Canadian unwrought nickel, scrap and powders are Free, with or without a USMCA claim. Canadian nickel semis are Free with a USMCA claim, or pay their base rate plus 10% without one. No Section 232 or Section 338 duty reaches nickel. Canada is the largest supplier: $1.02B of Chapter 75 goods in 2025, including $785M of unwrought nickel.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on nickel from China?
faqs.answer: 25% Section 301 (List 3) on every Chapter 75 line, including unwrought nickel, scrap and powders. Bars, wire, sheet, tube and fittings also pay the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty and their base rate: 39.5% to 40.5%.

faqs.question: Can the U.S. import Russian nickel?
faqs.answer: Not if it was produced on or after April 13, 2024: OFAC applied the import prohibition of Executive Order 14068 to nickel of Russian Federation origin on April 12, 2024, unless licensed. Older Russian nickel pays 35% in lieu of column 2 on unwrought nickel and powders and column 2 rates plus 12.5% on semis. The U.S. recorded no Chapter 75 imports from Russia in 2025.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. get its nickel?
searchedAs: where does the us get nickel from
where does the us get most of its nickel
how much nickel does the us import
faqs.answer: In 2025 the U.S. imported $3.37B of Chapter 75 nickel products. The largest suppliers were Canada $1.02B (30%), United Kingdom $368M (11%), Germany $254M (8%), France $248M (7%), Norway $236M (7%). Unwrought nickel was $1.39B, led by Canada and Norway. Nickel ores (Chapter 26) and nickel in stainless steel are not included.

faqs.question: What is HTS Chapter 75?
faqs.answer: Chapter 75 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule covers nickel and articles of nickel: mattes and oxide sinters (7501), unwrought nickel (7502), scrap (7503), powders and flakes (7504), bars, rods, profiles and wire (7505), plates, sheets, strip and foil (7506), tubes, pipes and fittings (7507) and other articles (7508): 29 ten-digit lines with base rates from Free to 3%.
